text:
Alicia: Heads-up — reproducer for weird memory growth during long contexts when paged KV is active. Seen on H100+A100 mix in the lab. Pattern: steady resident set until ~250k tokens, then a ~2–3GB climb and sustained higher GPU mem even after context free.

Alicia: Quick summary of signals: high PCIe stall cycles, repeated PT remap spikes, and a bunch of evict/reclaim churn in the kvcache logs. Not a 1-shot leak — looks like reuse window expansion + fragment reallocation.

Alicia: Dumped some logs from the run: 
```
[2026-03-10T15:22:18Z] kvcache: evict slot 0x3f8 -> page 412 (owner gpu:1)
[2026-03-10T15:22:18Z] kvcache: remap page 412 -> gpu:0 (dst ptr 0x7f9)
[2026-03-10T15:22:18Z] pagetable: seq 45233 reuse_window +1 (holes=7)
[2026-03-10T15:22:19Z] dma: pcie stall detected, 22ms
[2026-03-10T15:22:19Z] kvcache: alloc page 412 new frag id 99
```

Alicia: The odd bit is the repeated remap of the same page id across GPUs which matches the PCIe stalls. Hypothesis: page-table shadow remap is losing affinity and we then pay PCIe to move KV fragments around instead of reusing local slots.

Ben: Can you paste the perf counters / nvprof snippet you grabbed? Also which driver version?

Alicia: Driver 535.54.03 on the H100 nodes. nvprof excerpt: 
```
GPU 0: memcpy HtoD 3.1ms, kernel paged_attn_forward 0.45ms, memcpy DtoH 0.9ms
GPU 1: memcpy HtoD 25ms, paged_attn_forward 0.48ms, memcpy DtoH 24ms
NVTX: seq remap spikes align w/ memcpy on GPU1
```

Alicia: Also saw `cudaMemGetInfo` showing less free mem after loops even though logical refs dropped — suggests fragmentation.

Chun: Re: remap — did you see negative refcounts or wrapping in the PT owner table? We previously hit a wrap bug when seq numbers overflowed on long-lived sessions.

Alicia: No negative refs, but sequence numbers jump non-monotonic when two threads race eviction on the same page id. Attached small trace (excerpt): `pt_owner[412] before={owner:1,seq:45233} race -> after={owner:0,seq:45212}` — seq decreased.

Chun: That explains the reuse window blow-up. If seq goes backward the reuse set logic treats it as new cold page and avoids reuse, causing more allocations and fragmentation. We should treat seq as monotonic and ignore backward updates unless epoch advanced.

Frank: Tested a quick repro on RTX6000 and the pattern is different: less PCIe penalty (topology local) but fragmentation still grows. On A100-only nodes the remap is rarer, but when it happens eviction order is LIFO-ish so we still end up with holes.

Geeta: Proposed mitigation: 1) clamp PT seq updates so they never decrease; 2) prefer in-place reuse if owner==local and recent; 3) short-term pin of pages with high reuse score to avoid PCIe round-trip. Patch sketch: 
```
// clamp seq
if (new_seq < pt_owner[p].seq) new_seq = pt_owner[p].seq;
// prefer local reuse
if (pt_owner[p].owner == local_gpu && reuse_score > THRESH) return reuse_local(p);
```

Geeta: Also added an integration test `kvcache/longctx_reuse_smoke.sh` that runs 1M token synth with varying batch sizes, will push to CI.

Ben: Nice. Can we add a metric in telemetry: "pt_seq_backward" counter and "remote_remap_ms" so we can alert before user-visible mem growth?

DevOps Bot: deploy: rolling canary to h100-staging with kvcache/seq-clamp branch started by @Geeta at 2026-03-11T09:04:00Z :rocket: 

Frank: After applying the seq-clamp locally, reran the longctx synth. Memory stable now for 1M tokens (no steady climb). Still seeing a few small fragments but far less churn.

Alicia: Repro failure case for the old behavior is in `~/bugs/paged-kv-repro/2081122334/` — includes the JSON trace and `nvprof` captures. Pushing the repro and a short README.

Chun: Will follow up to harden PT update path (epoch-tagging + seq monotonicity). Also want to look at A100 eviction order — might need hybrid eviction policy (age + adjacency).

Geeta: Filed bug UI-3921 with logs and patch link. Recommend bumping the staging canary to 24h before prod.

Ben: Thanks all. Agreement: land seq-clamp + telemetry, add pin heuristic for hot pages, run 24h canary on H100 pool.

Alicia: FYI, added a unit test that simulates concurrent evict/remap and checks seq monotonicity. Quick pass here. :thumbsup:
